about: The condition context the game hands to every stats condition it evaluates (a spell's SpellRoll, a status's OnApplyRoll or RemoveConditions, a functor's condition): who acts, on whom, with what hit and which status. It lives on the caller's stack for the length of the evaluation, so it is readable at the moment of any roll the condition makes.

evidence.says: code:ls::thoth::shared::ContextData::ContextData writes its first entity argument here; code:unplaced::EvaluateStatusCondition passes the status's StatusCause as that argument

read at the moment of the roll through Ext.Events.Roll: Sacred Flame's save and Fire Bolt's attack show the caster here; a goblin's weapon attack shows the goblin; HOLD_PERSON's repeat save shows the held creature
code:ls::thoth::shared::ContextData::ContextData writes its second entity argument here; code:unplaced::EvaluateStatusCondition passes the status's Target as that argument

read at the moment of the roll through Ext.Events.Roll: Sacred Flame's save and Fire Bolt's attack show the goblin aimed at here; a goblin's weapon attack shows the struck creature (the host, or a third creature it attacked); HOLD_PERSON's repeat save shows the held creature

read at the moment of the roll through Ext.Events.Roll: HOLD_PERSON's repeat save shows HOLD_PERSON's FixedString here; it is empty (0xFFFFFFFF) for spell rolls

the macOS build's symbols and EoCShared.dll's exports hold the type's name in its constructors and in the argument lists of Machine::CheckStaticCondition and code:eoc::spell::CheckModifiableSpellRollCondition, which take it; it is tied to this layout by the constructor read here and by the context those functions are handed at a roll

code:ls::thoth::shared::ContextData::ContextData writes its first two entity arguments at +0x0 and +0x10, two vec3 at +0x40 and +0x4C, a HitDesc pointer at +0x68, a second pointer at +0xC8 and a FixedString at +0xD4

read at the moment of the roll through Ext.Events.Roll, at Sacred Flame's save, Fire Bolt's attack, a goblin's weapon attack and HOLD_PERSON's repeat save: the source at +0x0, the target at +0x10, the status's FixedString at +0xD4

questions.ask: +0x38 held the attacker's equipped weapon (one goblin attack); +0x70 is a 16-byte GUID shared by the attack and its damage (the cast's?); +0xD0 is a uint32 the status path sets to 1 (EStatusEvent?). Watch each, and the two positions and the two pointers the constructor fills, with a cast from an item, a thrown weapon and a status with a source.
